paragraphs.title: Sin Through Ignorance and the Lord’s Command

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses commanded to speak?
answers: The priests only
The children of Israel
The kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Speak unto the children of Israel.”

easy.question: What kind of sin is described in the verse?
answers: A deliberate sin
A sin committed out of fear
A sin committed through ignorance
easy.explanation: The phrase “through ignorance” describes a sin committed unintentionally.

medium.question: What condition is described for this kind of sin?
answers: A person breaks a commandment unintentionally
A person does not know Moses
A person immediately brings an offering
medium.explanation: The verse describes someone sinning through ignorance against one of the Lord’s commandments.

medium.question: What does “through ignorance” mean in the phrase “If a soul shall sin through ignorance”?
answers: Deliberately
Unintentionally
Secretly
medium.explanation: In this context, “through ignorance” means by mistake or without intending to sin.

medium.question: What does the order of the verses teach about passing on the message?
answers: Israel spoke to Moses, and Moses spoke to the Lord
Moses spoke to Israel without receiving a command
The Lord commanded Moses, and Moses was to speak to Israel
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses, and then commands him to speak to the children of Israel.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “the commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done”?
answers: They refer to commandments forbidding certain actions
They refer only to commandments about festivals
They refer to commandments that must always be performed
challenge.explanation: “Things which ought not to be done” refers to prohibited actions.

challenge.question: Why does the verse specify that the sin was committed “through ignorance”?
answers: To show that the person was a priest
To distinguish an accidental offense from a deliberate one
To say that the sin happened at night
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offense was unintentional rather than deliberate.

challenge.question: What precise detail is given about the number of commandments that may have been broken?
answers: Only one particular commandment
All the commandments at once
One of the forbidden commandments
challenge.explanation: The verse says the person has done against “any of them,” meaning one of the prohibited commandments.

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “the commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done”?
answers: They refer to commandments forbidding certain actions
They refer only to commandments about festivals
They refer to commandments that must always be performed
questions.explanation: “Things which ought not to be done” refers to prohibited actions.

questions.question: Why does the verse specify that the sin was committed “through ignorance”?
answers: To show that the person was a priest
To distinguish an accidental offense from a deliberate one
To say that the sin happened at night
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offense was unintentional rather than deliberate.

questions.question: What precise detail is given about the number of commandments that may have been broken?
answers: Only one particular commandment
All the commandments at once
One of the forbidden commandments
questions.explanation: The verse says the person has done against “any of them,” meaning one of the prohibited commandments.

easy.question: Who sinned according to these verses?
answers: The anointed priest
The whole people
The sons of Aaron
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “If the priest that is anointed do sin.”

easy.question: What animal was brought as the offering?
answers: A male lamb without blemish
A young bullock without blemish
A female goat
easy.explanation: The priest was to bring “a young bullock without blemish.”

easy.question: Where was the bullock killed?
answers: Outside the camp
On the altar of burnt offering
Before the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says that the bullock was killed “before the Lord.”

medium.question: What did the priest do after bringing the bullock to the door of the tabernacle?
answers: He laid his hand on its head and killed it
He poured its blood at the bottom of the altar
He sprinkled its blood seven times
medium.explanation: The order is bringing the bullock, laying a hand on its head, and then killing it.

medium.question: In the phrase “shall lay his hand upon the bullock’s head,” what action is described?
answers: He lifted his hand
He placed his hand
He washed his hand
medium.explanation: The phrase describes placing the priest’s hand on the bullock’s head.

medium.question: What did the priest do first after taking some of the bullock’s blood?
answers: He put the blood on the altar’s horns
He poured all the blood at the altar’s bottom
He brought the blood into the tabernacle
medium.explanation: First he brought the blood to the tabernacle; afterward he sprinkled and applied it.

challenge.question: What was done with the bullock’s blood?
answers: Some was put on the horns of the incense altar, and the rest was poured at the bottom of the burnt-offering altar
All of it was sprinkled only on the veil
All of it was poured outside the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes the blood placed on the incense altar’s horns from the rest, which was poured at the bottom of the burnt-offering altar.

challenge.question: What precise detail is given about the sprinkling of the blood?
answers: It was sprinkled three times on the altar
It was sprinkled seven times before the Lord, before the veil
It was sprinkled once on the bullock’s head
challenge.explanation: The priest dipped his finger in the blood and sprinkled it seven times before the Lord, before the veil.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the priest performing these actions before the Lord and in the tabernacle?
answers: The ritual had no fixed order
The offering was only for the priest to eat
The actions were sacred service performed in the Lord’s presence
challenge.explanation: The references to the Lord and the tabernacle show that this was an orderly act of sacred service.

questions.question: What was done with the bullock’s blood?
answers: Some was put on the horns of the incense altar, and the rest was poured at the bottom of the burnt-offering altar
All of it was sprinkled only on the veil
All of it was poured outside the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes the blood placed on the incense altar’s horns from the rest, which was poured at the bottom of the burnt-offering altar.

questions.question: What precise detail is given about the sprinkling of the blood?
answers: It was sprinkled three times on the altar
It was sprinkled seven times before the Lord, before the veil
It was sprinkled once on the bullock’s head
questions.explanation: The priest dipped his finger in the blood and sprinkled it seven times before the Lord, before the veil.

questions.question: What can be understood from the priest performing these actions before the Lord and in the tabernacle?
answers: The ritual had no fixed order
The offering was only for the priest to eat
The actions were sacred service performed in the Lord’s presence
questions.explanation: The references to the Lord and the tabernacle show that this was an orderly act of sacred service.

paragraphs.title: Burning the Fat and the Bullock

easy.question: What was removed from the bullock at the beginning of the process?
answers: All its fat
Only its skin
Only its head
easy.explanation: The passage says, “He shall take off from it all the fat of the bullock.”

easy.question: Who burned the bullock’s parts on the altar?
answers: The ruler
The priest
All the people
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the priest shall burn them upon the altar.”

easy.question: Where was the rest of the bullock taken?
answers: Into the tabernacle
To the altar
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The whole bullock was carried “without the camp.”

medium.question: What was done with the fat, kidneys, and the part above the liver?
answers: They were burned on the altar
They were buried in the camp
They were left on the bullock
medium.explanation: These parts were removed and burned on the altar of burnt offering.

medium.question: What part is mentioned in the phrase “the caul above the liver”?
answers: The bullock’s skin
The part attached to or above the liver
The blood inside the bullock
medium.explanation: The verse identifies the caul as a part associated with the liver and removed with the kidneys.

medium.question: What was the general order of the actions?
answers: The whole bullock was burned in the camp, and its ashes were taken out
The bullock was taken out, and then burned outside the camp
The whole bullock was burned on the altar
medium.explanation: The bullock was first carried outside the camp and then burned there on wood.

challenge.question: What distinction between the parts of the bullock is described?
answers: The fat was burned on the altar, while the rest was burned outside the camp
The whole bullock was burned on the altar
Only the skin was burned, and the rest was eaten
challenge.explanation: The fat and internal parts were burned on the altar, while the remaining bullock was taken outside the camp and burned.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “unto a clean place”?
answers: The burning took place in a random location
The place outside the camp still had to be clean
The bullock was later returned to the camp
challenge.explanation: Although the bullock was taken outside the camp, it still had to be brought to a clean place.

challenge.question: What easily overlooked detail appears at the end of the passage?
answers: The bullock was burned on the altar of burnt offering
It was burned on wood with fire, where the ashes were poured out
The bullock was burned inside the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The passage says it was burned on wood with fire where the ashes were poured out.

questions.question: What distinction between the parts of the bullock is described?
answers: The fat was burned on the altar, while the rest was burned outside the camp
The whole bullock was burned on the altar
Only the skin was burned, and the rest was eaten
questions.explanation: The fat and internal parts were burned on the altar, while the remaining bullock was taken outside the camp and burned.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “unto a clean place”?
answers: The burning took place in a random location
The place outside the camp still had to be clean
The bullock was later returned to the camp
questions.explanation: Although the bullock was taken outside the camp, it still had to be brought to a clean place.

questions.question: What easily overlooked detail appears at the end of the passage?
answers: The bullock was burned on the altar of burnt offering
It was burned on wood with fire, where the ashes were poured out
The bullock was burned inside the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The passage says it was burned on wood with fire where the ashes were poured out.

paragraphs.title: The Sin Offering of the Whole Congregation

easy.question: Who sinned through ignorance according to these verses?
answers: The whole congregation of Israel
The priest alone
The elders alone
easy.explanation: The passage says, “If the whole congregation of Israel sin through ignorance.”

easy.question: What animal was offered for the congregation’s sin?
answers: A lamb
A young bullock
A male goat
easy.explanation: The congregation was to offer a young bullock for a sin offering.

easy.question: Where was the bullock taken afterward?
answers: Into the tabernacle
To the top of the altar
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The bullock was carried outside the camp and burned there.

medium.question: What happened after the congregation’s sin became known?
answers: The congregation offered a bullock for a sin offering
The priest left the camp
The elders burned the altar
medium.explanation: Once the sin was known, the congregation was required to bring a young bullock to the tabernacle.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the thing be hid from the eyes of the assembly” mean?
answers: The matter was forgotten by the priest
The matter was not known or recognized
The matter was taken outside the camp
medium.explanation: The context shows that the sin was not initially known or noticed by the assembly.

medium.question: What did the priest do after sprinkling the blood seven times?
answers: He immediately burned the bullock
He carried the bullock outside the camp
He put some of the blood on the altar’s horns
medium.explanation: After the sprinkling, the priest put some of the blood on the horns of the altar.

challenge.question: What was done with the remaining blood after some was put on the altar’s horns?
answers: It was poured at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering
It was burned outside the camp
It was returned to the bullock’s head
challenge.explanation: The passage says that all the remaining blood was poured at the bottom of the altar.

challenge.question: What was the result after the priest made atonement for the congregation?
answers: The bullock remained inside the camp
They were forgiven
The elders offered another sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says, “the priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.”

challenge.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Burning the bullock, sprinkling, killing
Killing, burning, laying on hands
Laying on hands, killing the bullock, handling its blood
challenge.explanation: The elders laid their hands on the bullock, it was killed, and then the priest handled its blood.

questions.question: What was done with the remaining blood after some was put on the altar’s horns?
answers: It was poured at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering
It was burned outside the camp
It was returned to the bullock’s head
questions.explanation: The passage says that all the remaining blood was poured at the bottom of the altar.

questions.question: What was the result after the priest made atonement for the congregation?
answers: The bullock remained inside the camp
They were forgiven
The elders offered another sacrifice
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says, “the priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.”

questions.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Burning the bullock, sprinkling, killing
Killing, burning, laying on hands
Laying on hands, killing the bullock, handling its blood
questions.explanation: The elders laid their hands on the bullock, it was killed, and then the priest handled its blood.

paragraphs.title: The Sin Offering of a Ruler

easy.question: Who is described at the beginning of the passage as sinning?
answers: The priest
The ruler
A poor person
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “When a ruler hath sinned.”

easy.question: What animal did the ruler bring as an offering?
answers: A male goat without blemish
A female lamb
Two doves
easy.explanation: The ruler was to bring “a kid of the goats, a male without blemish.”

easy.question: What did the priest do with the blood of the sin offering?
answers: He poured it all outside the camp
He put some of it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering
He smeared it on the ruler’s head
easy.explanation: The priest put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering.

medium.question: What caused the ruler to bring the offering?
answers: He made a special vow
He won a war
His sin came to his knowledge
medium.explanation: When the ruler became aware of his sin, he brought the required offering.

medium.question: What kind of person is described by the word “ruler” in this passage?
answers: A leader or governor
A sick person
A temple servant
medium.explanation: The passage concerns a person in a position of leadership or authority.

medium.question: What order of actions is described for the offering?
answers: Burning the fat, laying on hands, then killing
Killing, laying on hands, then bringing the offering
Laying on hands, killing, then the priest handling the blood
medium.explanation: The ruler laid his hand on the goat, it was killed, and then the priest handled its blood.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the fact that even a ruler had to bring an offering for his sin?
answers: His position did not exempt him from responsibility
Only rulers were allowed to sin
The ruler did not need atonement
challenge.explanation: The passage teaches that a leader too must deal with his sin and seek atonement.

challenge.question: What distinction is made between the blood and the fat of the offering?
answers: The blood was poured at the altar’s base, while the fat was burned
The blood was burned, while the fat was poured at the altar’s base
Both the blood and fat were put on the altar’s horns
challenge.explanation: The blood was applied to the altar and poured at its base, while all the fat was burned on the altar.

challenge.question: What was the main condition of the sin for which the offering was brought?
answers: It was deliberate
It was committed through ignorance
It was committed by a foreigner
challenge.explanation: The ruler sinned through ignorance, yet still needed an offering and forgiveness.

questions.question: What can be understood from the fact that even a ruler had to bring an offering for his sin?
answers: His position did not exempt him from responsibility
Only rulers were allowed to sin
The ruler did not need atonement
questions.explanation: The passage teaches that a leader too must deal with his sin and seek atonement.

questions.question: What distinction is made between the blood and the fat of the offering?
answers: The blood was poured at the altar’s base, while the fat was burned
The blood was burned, while the fat was poured at the altar’s base
Both the blood and fat were put on the altar’s horns
questions.explanation: The blood was applied to the altar and poured at its base, while all the fat was burned on the altar.

questions.question: What was the main condition of the sin for which the offering was brought?
answers: It was deliberate
It was committed through ignorance
It was committed by a foreigner
questions.explanation: The ruler sinned through ignorance, yet still needed an offering and forgiveness.

paragraphs.title: The Sin Offering of an Ordinary Israelite

easy.question: Who is described as sinning through ignorance?
answers: One of the common people
The high priest
The whole people together
easy.explanation: The passage describes one person among the common people who sins through ignorance.

easy.question: What offering was the person to bring?
answers: A male ram
A female goat without blemish
Two doves
easy.explanation: The passage requires a female goat without blemish.

easy.question: What did the priest do with the offering’s blood?
answers: He burned it all on the altar
He poured it all on the ground
He put some on the altar’s horns and poured the rest at its base
easy.explanation: The priest applied some blood to the altar’s horns and poured the rest at the bottom of the altar.

medium.question: What happened after the person became aware of the sin?
answers: He ignored it
He brought his offering
He immediately burned the altar
medium.explanation: After learning of the sin, he brought a female goat without blemish as an offering.

medium.question: What does “without blemish” mean in this context?
answers: Very large
Fast
Whole and free from defect
medium.explanation: The phrase describes an animal suitable for sacrifice, without any defect or blemish.

medium.question: Why did the person bring an offering?
answers: Because he sinned through ignorance against a forbidden commandment
Because he wanted to give thanks for a good harvest
Because the priest commanded it without reference to sin
medium.explanation: The offering was brought because the person unintentionally violated one of the Lord’s commandments.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in the place of the burnt offering”?
answers: The offering was burned outside the camp
It was offered at the place designated for the burnt-offering altar
It was itself a burnt offering
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the place of slaughter; it does not change the type of offering.

challenge.question: Which action belonged to the sinner rather than the priest?
answers: Laying a hand on the head of the sin offering
Putting the blood on the altar’s horns
Pouring the remaining blood at the altar’s base
challenge.explanation: The person laid a hand on the offering, while the priest handled its blood.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of actions?
answers: Killing, bringing the offering, laying on hands, applying the blood
Applying the blood, laying on hands, killing, bringing the offering
Bringing the offering, laying on hands, killing, and the priest handling the blood
challenge.explanation: The person brought the offering, laid a hand on it, and killed it; then the priest handled the blood.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in the place of the burnt offering”?
answers: The offering was burned outside the camp
It was offered at the place designated for the burnt-offering altar
It was itself a burnt offering
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the place of slaughter; it does not change the type of offering.

questions.question: Which action belonged to the sinner rather than the priest?
answers: Laying a hand on the head of the sin offering
Putting the blood on the altar’s horns
Pouring the remaining blood at the altar’s base
questions.explanation: The person laid a hand on the offering, while the priest handled its blood.

questions.question: What is the correct order of actions?
answers: Killing, bringing the offering, laying on hands, applying the blood
Applying the blood, laying on hands, killing, bringing the offering
Bringing the offering, laying on hands, killing, and the priest handling the blood
questions.explanation: The person brought the offering, laid a hand on it, and killed it; then the priest handled the blood.

paragraphs.title: Burning the Fat and Making Atonement

easy.question: What was removed from the offering?
answers: All its fat
All its blood
All its flesh
easy.explanation: The verse says, “he shall take away all the fat thereof.”

easy.question: Who burned the fat on the altar?
answers: The person bringing the offering
The priest
The Levites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the priest shall burn it upon the altar.”

easy.question: What result is described at the end of the verse?
answers: The offering was immediately eaten
The priest left the sanctuary
The sinner was forgiven
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “it shall be forgiven him.”

medium.question: What was the removal of the fat compared with?
answers: The removal of the fat from the sacrifice of peace offerings
Washing the offering with water
Removing the blood from the offering
medium.explanation: The verse compares the action to removing the fat from a peace offering.

medium.question: What is the order of actions described?
answers: Atonement, removal of the fat, burning
Removal of the fat, burning, atonement
Burning, atonement, removal of the fat
medium.explanation: First the fat was removed, then the priest burned it, and afterward made atonement.

medium.question: What does “a sweet savour unto the Lord” indicate in this context?
answers: The priest had to smell the offering
The burning was acceptable to the Lord
The smoke had to remain on the altar
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the offering as pleasing and acceptable before the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “as the fat is taken away from off the sacrifice of peace offerings”?
answers: This offering was handled in a way similar to a peace offering
It was forbidden to burn its fat
The offering itself was a peace offering
challenge.explanation: The comparison teaches that the fat was removed in the same general manner as in a peace offering.

challenge.question: What does “a sweet savour unto the Lord” express in the description of the burning?
answers: The priest had to smell the offering
The burning was considered acceptable before the Lord
The smoke had to remain on the altar
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the offering as pleasing and acceptable to the Lord, not merely as a physical smell.

challenge.question: What cause-and-effect relationship stands out at the end of the verse?
answers: The fat was removed, so the offering was eaten
The priest made atonement, so the offering was burned
After the priest’s service came atonement and forgiveness
challenge.explanation: The priest burned the fat and made atonement, after which the verse says the sinner was forgiven.

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “as the fat is taken away from off the sacrifice of peace offerings”?
answers: This offering was handled in a way similar to a peace offering
It was forbidden to burn its fat
The offering itself was a peace offering
questions.explanation: The comparison teaches that the fat was removed in the same general manner as in a peace offering.

questions.question: What does “a sweet savour unto the Lord” express in the description of the burning?
answers: The priest had to smell the offering
The burning was considered acceptable before the Lord
The smoke had to remain on the altar
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the offering as pleasing and acceptable to the Lord, not merely as a physical smell.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect relationship stands out at the end of the verse?
answers: The fat was removed, so the offering was eaten
The priest made atonement, so the offering was burned
After the priest’s service came atonement and forgiveness
questions.explanation: The priest burned the fat and made atonement, after which the verse says the sinner was forgiven.

paragraphs.title: Bringing the Ewe and Laying on Hands

easy.question: What animal was brought as a sin offering?
answers: A female lamb
A goat
A bullock
easy.explanation: The passage says, “If he bring a lamb for a sin offering,” and specifies a female.

easy.question: What quality was required of the lamb?
answers: It had to be large
It had to be without blemish
It had to be young
easy.explanation: The offering had to be a female lamb without blemish.

easy.question: What did the person do before killing the offering?
answers: He laid his hand on its head
He placed it on the altar
He gave it to the priest
easy.explanation: The person laid his hand on the head of the sin offering before killing it.

medium.question: What is the order of actions described?
answers: Killing, bringing, laying on hands
Bringing the offering, laying on hands, killing
Laying on hands, burning, bringing
medium.explanation: The lamb was brought first, then the person laid a hand on it, and finally it was killed.

medium.question: Where was the lamb to be killed?
answers: Outside the camp
At the offerer’s house
At the place where the burnt offering was killed
medium.explanation: The verse says it was to be killed where they killed the burnt offering.

medium.question: What does “without blemish” mean in the phrase “a female without blemish”?
answers: Free from defect
Very large
White in color
medium.explanation: The phrase describes an animal that was whole and without any defect.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “where they kill the burnt offering”?
answers: The sin offering and burnt offering had a common place of slaughter
The lamb became a burnt offering
Both offerings had to be sacrificed together
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies a shared place of slaughter; it does not turn the sin offering into a burnt offering.

challenge.question: What does “it” refer to in “and slay it for a sin offering”?
answers: The offerer’s hand
The female lamb that was brought as the sin offering
The burnt offering mentioned at the end
challenge.explanation: The pronoun refers to the female lamb brought as the sin offering.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by calling the offering a “sin offering” both when it is brought and when it is killed?
answers: It remained a sin offering throughout the process
It was ultimately intended as a burnt offering
The offerer had to bring two lambs
challenge.explanation: The repeated designation makes clear that the lamb was brought and killed as a sin offering, even though it was killed at the burnt offering’s location.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “where they kill the burnt offering”?
answers: The sin offering and burnt offering had a common place of slaughter
The lamb became a burnt offering
Both offerings had to be sacrificed together
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies a shared place of slaughter; it does not turn the sin offering into a burnt offering.

questions.question: What does “it” refer to in “and slay it for a sin offering”?
answers: The offerer’s hand
The female lamb that was brought as the sin offering
The burnt offering mentioned at the end
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to the female lamb brought as the sin offering.

questions.question: What is emphasized by calling the offering a “sin offering” both when it is brought and when it is killed?
answers: It remained a sin offering throughout the process
It was ultimately intended as a burnt offering
The offerer had to bring two lambs
questions.explanation: The repeated designation makes clear that the lamb was brought and killed as a sin offering, even though it was killed at the burnt offering’s location.

paragraphs.title: Applying the Blood and Completing the Atonement

easy.question: What did the priest take with his finger?
answers: Some of the sin offering’s blood
Some water
Some incense
easy.explanation: The verse says that the priest took some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger.

easy.question: Where did the priest put the blood?
answers: On the priest’s garments
On the horns of the altar of burnt offering
On the floor of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The priest put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering.

easy.question: What happened after atonement was made for the sin?
answers: The offering was returned home
The priest left the camp
The sinner was forgiven
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “it shall be forgiven him.”

medium.question: What did the priest do with all the remaining blood after putting some on the altar’s horns?
answers: He poured it at the bottom of the altar
He kept it in a vessel
He burned it outside the camp
medium.explanation: After applying some blood to the horns, the priest poured all the remaining blood at the altar’s bottom.

medium.question: What does “the bottom of the altar” refer to?
answers: The altar’s upper decoration
The base of the altar
A vessel inside the altar
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the lower part or base of the altar.

medium.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Burning the fat, applying the blood, pouring the blood
Pouring the blood, burning the fat, taking the blood
Applying the blood to the altar’s horns, pouring the remaining blood, burning the fat
medium.explanation: The blood was first applied to the horns, the rest was poured at the altar’s base, and the fat was then burned.

challenge.question: Why does the verse say that the fat was removed “as the fat of the lamb is taken away from the sacrifice of the peace offerings”?
answers: To compare the procedure with the familiar rule for peace offerings
To teach that this was a peace offering
To say that the lamb was offered in place of the sin offering
challenge.explanation: The verse uses the peace offering as a comparison for how the fat was to be removed, without changing the type of offering.

challenge.question: What distinction is made between the blood and the fat?
answers: Both the blood and fat were put on the altar’s horns
The blood was poured at the altar’s base, while the fat was burned on the altar
The blood was burned, while the fat was poured at the altar’s base
challenge.explanation: The blood was applied to the horns and poured at the altar’s base, while the fat was removed and burned.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the priest’s actions and the result at the end of the passage?
answers: The actions moved the offering to another place
The actions removed the need for a priest
After the priest performed the service, atonement and forgiveness were declared
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes that the priest made atonement and that the sinner was forgiven.

questions.question: Why does the verse say that the fat was removed “as the fat of the lamb is taken away from the sacrifice of the peace offerings”?
answers: To compare the procedure with the familiar rule for peace offerings
To teach that this was a peace offering
To say that the lamb was offered in place of the sin offering
questions.explanation: The verse uses the peace offering as a comparison for how the fat was to be removed, without changing the type of offering.

questions.question: What distinction is made between the blood and the fat?
answers: Both the blood and fat were put on the altar’s horns
The blood was poured at the altar’s base, while the fat was burned on the altar
The blood was burned, while the fat was poured at the altar’s base
